Whether alia-console is intended to survive as an Alia product surface or be absorbed into Oxy Console is a PRODUCT decision that this read-only inventory cannot make. Every console classification below is a recommendation with its reasoning stated, not a finding.

The 'exposesProviderSecret' flag distinguishes a PROVIDER credential (an upstream inference vendor's key) from a FIRST-PARTY Alia developer key. alia-console shows keyPrefix for the latter, which is by design and is not a provider secret. If the epic's threat model treats any key prefix as sensitive, four console screens change classification.

items.name: Console — Dashboard
items.summary: Developer landing page: aggregate app/key/request stats plus the credit balance. Calls GET /developer/stats and GET /credits/.
items.removalGate: Oxy Console has a developer landing surface. Nothing here is provider-aware, so this is a relocation for consistency, not a decoupling requirement — it can move last.

items.name: Console — Playground
items.summary: Interactive chat playground: model picker fed by GET /models/stats, temperature and max-tokens controls, streaming POST to /v1/chat/completions. Default model is the literal 'route:instant'.
items.removalGate: Keep as an Alia product surface wherever the console lands — it exercises the public Alia inference API and must keep showing Alia aliases only. The one hard-coded default (:103) should read from the fetched list instead.

items.name: Console — Models
items.summary: Read-only Alia model catalog with latency, uptime, success rate, credit multiplier, max tokens and tool/vision flags. Renders only Alia ids and tiers — no provider column.
items.removalGate: Keep. This is the correct pattern for the whole epic: an Alia-branded catalog with health metrics and zero provider identity, entirely driven by GET /models/stats. Preserve that contract — the moment /models/stats gains a provider field this screen leaks it.

items.name: Console — Usage
items.summary: Workspace-wide developer usage over a selectable period. GET /developer/usage.
items.removalGate: Oxy Console serves developer usage for Alia-issued keys. Distinct from ga-screen-usage (upstream COGS) — do not merge the two.

items.name: Console — Billing
items.summary: Customer billing: credit balance, credit packs, Alia subscription plans, transaction history, Stripe checkout for both credits and subscriptions. Product is hard-coded to 'alia'.
items.removalGate: Oxy Console owns billing for Oxy products AND the plans/packages this screen reads are administered somewhere (see ga-screen-plans, ga-screen-credit-packages). Note the coupling: the ADMIN side of these same objects currently lives in the gateway admin, so the two must be planned together or the read side outlives its editor.

items.name: Console — Apps list
items.summary: List, create and delete developer apps (name, description, website URL).
items.removalGate: Oxy Console owns developer app registration. Nothing provider-aware.

items.name: Console — App detail (keys list)
items.summary: Per-app overview listing its Alia API keys; creates a key and copies the freshly minted value to the clipboard. Lists show only keyPrefix.
items.removalGate: Oxy Console owns first-party key issuance. The key here is an ALIA-issued customer credential (alia_sk_*), not an upstream provider key — so it is in scope for a normal developer console and must not be conflated with ga-screen-keys.

items.name: Console — App settings
items.summary: Edit an app's name, description and website URL. PATCH /developer/apps/:id.
items.removalGate: Moves with the apps list.

items.name: Console — App usage
items.summary: Per-app usage over a selectable period. GET /developer/apps/:id/usage.
items.removalGate: Moves with the apps list.

items.name: Console — API key detail
items.summary: Key metadata, scopes, 7-day usage, delete, and an env-var block presenting ALIA_API_KEY (masked to prefix) plus ALIA_BASE_URL.
items.removalGate: Moves with the apps list. Explicitly NOT a provider secret: the value shown is the caller's own Alia key prefix, and the base URL is api.alia.onl/v1. The clipboard action copies the PREFIX only, not a full key.

items.name: Console — Workspace settings
items.summary: Largest console screen (595 lines): workspace rename, avatar upload, member invite/remove/role-change, workspace delete. Talks to /organization/* — an Oxy org concept, not an Alia one.
items.removalGate: Oxy Console owns organizations and membership. Strongest move candidate in the console: it is already a pure Oxy-org CRUD screen that happens to be hosted in Alia, and the X-Workspace-Id header it drives is set globally in the console's API client.

items.name: Console — Examples
items.summary: Static copy-paste code samples (Python/Node/curl/function-calling) all using model 'route:auto' against api.alia.onl.
items.removalGate: Keep — it documents the Alia public API. It does name the OpenAI SDK as a client library (:47,63,120), which is a wire-format compatibility claim about the CLIENT, not a statement about who serves inference. Judgment call flagged, not a violation.

items.name: Console — Documentation index
items.summary: Landing page linking the five documentation sub-pages.
items.removalGate: Keep with the docs set.

items.name: Console — Docs: Quick Start
items.summary: First-request walkthrough using model 'route:auto'; installs the openai client package.
items.removalGate: Keep.

items.name: Console — Docs: Authentication
items.summary: Bearer-token auth guide with a curl sample using model 'route:auto'.
items.removalGate: Keep.

items.name: Console — Docs: Chat Completions
items.summary: Endpoint reference; the model parameter is documented by example as 'route:auto' / 'route:pro-standard'.
items.removalGate: Keep.

items.name: Console — Docs: Models
items.summary: HAND-MAINTAINED model catalog listing exactly four aliases (route:instant, route:auto, route:pro-standard, route:pro) as literal objects in the page source, while the API defines twelve.
items.removalGate: Keep the screen, but this is a real defect to fix during the epic: it duplicates the catalog rather than reading GET /models/stats like its sibling /models screen does, so it is already stale by eight aliases and will silently drift further as kaana takes over the catalog.

items.name: Console — Docs: SDKs
items.summary: SDK integration guide. Densest provider-name page in any Alia frontend: 15 occurrences of OpenAI/openai, including a section headed 'OpenAI SDK Compatibility' and an @ai-sdk/openai createOpenAI sample.
items.removalGate: Keep, but have a human rule on it explicitly. Every occurrence is about the CLIENT LIBRARY and the wire format ('point the OpenAI SDK at api.alia.onl'), which is a legitimate and commercially useful compatibility claim — it says nothing about who serves inference. It is nonetheless the page most likely to be read as a provider disclosure, so it deserves a decision on the record rather than a silent pass.

items.name: Console — / redirect
items.summary: 7-line route that redirects / to the dashboard. No UI.
items.removalGate: Moves with the dashboard. Listed for completeness so the console screen count reconciles against the route tree.

items.name: Console API client
items.summary: Axios instance against config.apiUrl (default https://api.alia.onl) with a bearer-token interceptor, an X-Workspace-Id header on every request, and a single 401 refresh-and-retry.
items.removalGate: Whatever host absorbs the console screens provides the equivalent client. Note it sets withCredentials: true (:11) despite the Oxy session model being device-first and zero-cookie — worth checking during the move, though it is not a provider-decoupling concern.

items.name: useModelsStats
items.summary: React Query hook over GET /models/stats. Its ModelStats interface is provider-free by construction (id, name, description, tier, category, creditMultiplier, latency, uptime, successRate, health, capability flags, maxTokens).
items.removalGate: Keep. This hook plus its DTO is the contract that keeps the console's two model screens abstraction-safe — treat the absence of a provider field in ModelStats as a load-bearing invariant and gate it, since nothing today would fail if a provider field were added.

items.name: App model picker
items.summary: The main Expo app's model dropdown. Fetches GET /v1/models?chat=true, caches in a module-level `let`, gates each entry against entitlements.allowedModelIds, and routes locked models to /subscribe. Carries four hard-coded alias literals as fallbacks.
items.removalGate: Keep — this is the user-facing picker and must stay Alia-branded and API-driven. Two things to fix while the epic is open: (a) the thinking-model detection is a substring test, modelId.includes('thinking') (:26,:36), which silently misclassifies any future alias containing that word; (b) `cachedModels` is a module-level mutable `let` read from render (:21,:98), which is exactly the external-mutable-state-in-a-memoized-position hazard the React Compiler rules warn about.

items.name: useModelStore (zustand, persisted)
items.summary: The only store slice holding model state: selectedModel and baseModel (last non-thinking model), both defaulting to the literal 'route:auto', persisted to AsyncStorage under the key 'chat-storage'.
items.removalGate: Keep. Flag for the epic: because the value is PERSISTED, retiring or renaming an alias strands every existing installation on a dead id with no migration path — the store has no validation against the fetched catalog. Verified this is the only model-holding store: the other 15 files in packages/app/lib/stores/ contain no model state.

items.name: CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVES downgrade map
items.summary: A hand-maintained 10-entry map from alias to a cheaper alias plus a credit multiplier, used to offer a one-tap model downgrade when credits run low. The densest hard-coded alias site in any Alia frontend.
items.removalGate: Keep the feature, but this map must become server-driven during the epic: it hard-codes both the alias graph AND the credit multipliers in a client, and it already omits two of the twelve defined aliases (route:instant and route:audio have no entry — correct for route:instant as the floor, unexamined for route:audio). Every alias change requires an app release to stay correct.

items.name: FREE_ENTITLEMENTS placeholder
items.summary: React Query placeholderData hard-coding the free tier's allowed aliases as ['route:instant','route:auto','route:audio'], duplicated verbatim at model-selector.tsx:104 and matching FREE_MODEL_IDS in two API files.
items.removalGate: Keep as a placeholder, but collapse the FOUR copies of this list to one. Measured duplicates: packages/app/src/features/billing/runtime/use-billing.ts:327, packages/app/components/model-selector.tsx:104, packages/api/src/internal/providers/lib/seed-plans.ts:33, packages/api/src/lib/plan-access.ts:12. They agree today; nothing enforces that they keep agreeing, and the two client copies decide what a user can select before the server answers.

items.name: Chat header / page-content / streaming model plumbing

items.name: App model API route constants
items.summary: Two route constants the app uses for model data: '/analytics/models' and '/v1/models'. The former feeds the credits panel's per-model breakdown.
items.removalGate: Keep. Both endpoints must keep returning Alia aliases only; /analytics/models is rendered directly to end users in the credits panel, so it is a live abstraction-leak surface if the API ever resolves a raw provider model id there.

items.name: @alia.onl/sdk model defaults
items.summary: The published SDK's model surface: a `model` prop defaulting to 'route:auto' (documented on AliaChatScreen and AliaChatSheet) plus two voice paths pinned to 'route:voice'. No model PICKER ships in the SDK — the consumer passes an id.
items.removalGate: Keep, and treat these three literals as the highest-inertia alias references in the repo: they are compiled into external consumers' apps (the package ships as RAW SOURCE), so retiring route:auto or route:voice breaks installed SDK versions that no Alia deploy can fix. Any alias retirement plan must keep both ids resolvable indefinitely or ship a major SDK version first. Verified there is no model picker component in the SDK: all 49 files under packages/alia-chat/src were enumerated.

items.name: Codea webview model picker
items.summary: In-editor chat model dropdown. Fetches the catalog from the API but ships a one-entry defaultModels fallback and a hard-coded initial state, both 'route:code'.
items.removalGate: Keep. Same shipped-binary inertia as the SDK: a VS Code extension in the marketplace keeps sending 'route:code' until each user updates.

items.name: Codea VS Code settings + providers
items.summary: The codea.model contributed setting defaults to 'route:code'; three extension entry points read it with the same literal as their fallback (chat participant, chat provider, inline completions).
items.removalGate: Keep. The setting is correctly documented as 'available models are fetched from the API', and it is a free-form string rather than an enum, so the catalog can grow without an extension release — only the DEFAULT is frozen. Also update packages/alia-codea/README.md:15,63, which list alias ids in prose.

items.name: Codea CLI model defaults
items.summary: Three commander --model options defaulting to 'route:code', plus the config default and the sessions fallback. The TUI strips the 'route:auto-' prefix for display.
items.removalGate: Keep. One defect to fix while here: the --model help text advertises short names ('codea, codea-pro, codea-thinking') while the default is a full alias id — the two vocabularies disagree, and 'codea-pro'/'codea-thinking' correspond to no defined alias. Also update packages/alia-codea-cli/README.md:125.

items.name: Canvas model list and workflow node defaults
items.summary: fetchModels() reads GET /v1/models with a one-entry 'route:instant' fallback; the workflow editor and node edit panel seed every AI node with 'route:instant'. Also exports a deprecated static MODELS alias of the fallback.
items.removalGate: Keep. Included because canvas was not named in the brief but carries six alias sites and its own /v1/models client — an alias-retirement sweep that skips it leaves saved workflow nodes pinned to a dead id. The `MODELS` export at models.ts:42 is a back-compat alias with a comment saying it will be replaced; it should be deleted rather than carried forward.

items.name: shared-types AliaTier union
items.summary: The declared canonical superset of Alia tiers (14 members) plus the AliaModel / ModelCapabilities DTOs. Explicitly documented as provider-agnostic by construction.
items.removalGate: Keep and make it authoritative. It calls itself 'the canonical superset', yet the gateway admin maintains a SECOND, DIFFERENT 12-member list (missing v1-tts and v1-image) with no type relationship between them. Retiring the gateway admin removes that fork for free — which is an argument for doing workstream 9 early rather than late.
